why: A local bound to a same-file call's result is another name for what the callee returned. mark: held() returns the receiver's own set and the candidate adds to it through the local; the lint refuses the candidate (alias-mutation), so no lemma is written, and lane B's witness stands. tag: the same add through view(), two calls from the field, is a refactor of the direct add; refused by the same rule, so lane A says nothing and lane B bounds it. grown: copy() returns fresh() which returns a spread copy of primitives, fresh through its callee; the push is admitted and proved (the heap core reads it, one allocation on each side). count: untouched, proved. Each unit runs through check.mjs, which translates the unit and its callees only, so an admitted unit is proved beside a refused one.
